text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Clinton is preparing a new strategy to save the peace process and get Israeli-Palestinian negotiations moving.

- The cabinet issued some important decrees on housing yesterday. Information Minister Safwat el-Sherif said government agencies would give back to their owners buildings they do not need. It will pay more rent on those it does need.
- President Hosni Mubarak had talks with Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs.
- The cabinet said Egypt remained committed to peace and demanded that Israel stop building in Jerusalem.

- Supply and Trade Minister Ahmed Gueily issued a decree that wheat deliveries to the state will be voluntary this season. He fixed the producer price at 95 pounds ($28) an ardab of 150 kg for wheat of all varieties if it is 22 degrees clean. For each extra half degree of cleanness, the state will pay an extra 3.15 pounds.

- Mubarak issued a decree calling voters to vote in local elections on April 7. An Interior Ministry official said there will be 264 voting committees supervised by about 13,000 members of the judiciary.
- A French tourist aged 60 was killed when she fell from on top of the Pharaonic temple at Dendera in southern Egypt.

- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa and presidential adviser Osama el-Baz said that an Israeli retreat from the measures it has taken in Jerusalem will be the starting point for saving the Middle East peace process.
- The Pakistani government has invited President Mubarak to visit Pakistan. The invitation was extended when the Pakistani chief of staff saw Mubarak yesterday.

- The cabinet endorsed a document which is entitled "21st Century Egypt" and which sets a goal of creating 11 million jobs and increasing the volume of Egyptian trade fourfold. The trade deficit should disappear at the end of the third five-year plan. The cabinet offered the document for widespread debate.

- The state's Holding Company for Metallurgical Industries made profits of 456 million pounds in the financial year which ended last June 30. The average wage of workers rose to 780 pounds a month, Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid said.
